acceptanceCriteria: A1: crates/cockpit-cli/tests/cli_mcp_outcome_parity.rs adds one new #[test] that spawns the real ai-cockpit binary as a subprocess for the CLI side and calls cockpit_mcp::handle_request_for_repo() in-process for the MCP side, against the identical temporary repository fixture and Work Item.

A2: the test asserts the CLI's work-item outcome --json stdout and the MCP work_item_outcome tool's structuredContent.outcome are exactly equal (serde_json::Value equality), using a RuntimeContext reconstructed to match the exact CLI binary under test so the comparison is not defeated by incidental runtime-identity differences.
A3: cargo test --locked -p cockpit-cli --test cli_mcp_outcome_parity passes.
A4: cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings pass for the new file.
A5: no existing test file is modified; no production source file is modified.
goal: A regression that makes the CLI and MCP Outcome representations diverge is caught automatically by cargo test, instead of relying on manual review to notice.
intent: Close the invariant-5 gap named in WI-681's coverage mapping (docs/reference/collaboration-invariant-coverage.md): add one new integration test that spawns the real ai-cockpit CLI binary as a subprocess and, in the same test, calls the production MCP handler in-process against the identical repository fixture, then asserts the two Outcome representations are exactly equal. This combines two already-proven existing test patterns (subprocess spawning from outcome_handoff.rs; MCP-handler-in-process calls from rpc.rs) rather than introducing new test infrastructure, per explicit repository-owner delegation to continue the AI Cockpit collaboration-language initiative.
outOfScope: any change to production code in crates/cockpit-cli/src
and 9 test gaps (separate follow-on Work Items named in WI-681)
